manifest.name: Auth Timeout
manifest.summary: Ask for authentication after user inactivity
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

models._description: Adds the timeout configuration: lock_timeout, lock_timeout_mfa, lock_timeout_inactivity, lock_timeout_inactivity_mfa (+ UI compute/inverse helpers) and the cached _get_lock_timeouts() resolver
relations: _inherit res.groups (timeout policy attached to access groups)
_inherit res.users (resolves timeouts from the user's implied groups)

models._description: Caps trusted-device age to the shortest MFA session timeout (_get_trusted_device_age)

behavioral_notes.observation: The whole module hangs off ir.http._authenticate, the per-request auth hook. After super()._authenticate, for any auth='user' route with a logged-in session it calls _must_check_identity(). That resolver pulls the user's timeouts (res.users._get_lock_timeouts) and walks two thresholds: a hard 'lock_timeout' compared against the session's create_time (max session age regardless of activity) and a 'lock_timeout_inactivity' compared against the session key 'identity-check-next'. threshold = time.time() - timeout; if the stored timestamp - first_timeout <= threshold the timeout is breached. A breached lock_timeout returns {logout:True} -> _authenticate raises SessionExpiredException (client redirects to /web/login, full re-login); a breached inactivity timeout returns {check_identity:True} -> raises the module's CheckIdentityException (a SessionExpiredException subclass with DEBUG loglevel) unless the route opted out via routing check_identity=False. So expiry is enforced lazily on the NEXT request after the deadline, not by a background job.

behavioral_notes.element: ir.http._set_session_inactivity + ir.websocket presence (how session activity is stamped)
behavioral_notes.observation: Inactivity is tracked not via an HTTP last-seen timestamp but through the bus websocket presence channel. ir.websocket._update_mail_presence (extended) forwards the JS-reported inactivity_period to ir.http._set_session_inactivity(session, inactivity_period): it converts ms->s, fetches the user's shortest inactivity timeout, and when inactive (period >= timeout, or force=True) writes session['identity-check-next'] = now + timeout - inactivity_period, persisting via root.session_store.save(session) because websocket requests don't auto-save the session. If the user becomes active again before the deadline it pops 'identity-check-next'. ir.websocket._on_websocket_closed calls _set_session_inactivity(session, force=True) so closing the last tab / losing connectivity immediately arms the deadline. Only the lowest inactivity timeout sets the key, so _must_check_identity discounts higher timeouts by 'first_timeout' to stay consistent.

behavioral_notes.element: res.groups timeout configuration + _get_lock_timeouts() resolver (configurable: group-scoped, not per-user)
behavioral_notes.observation: Timeouts are configured per access GROUP, not per individual user and not as a single system parameter: res.groups gains lock_timeout, lock_timeout_mfa, lock_timeout_inactivity, lock_timeout_inactivity_mfa (minutes), plus human-readable UI helpers (delay/unit selection, with_2fa vs without_2fa). The @ormcache('self._ids') _get_lock_timeouts() folds every group a user implies into the SHORTEST applicable timeout per type, splitting MFA vs non-MFA into ordered (seconds, requires_mfa) tuples; res.users._get_lock_timeouts resolves this through _get_group_ids(). create/write/unlink override env.registry.clear_cache() whenever any of the four core fields change to keep the ormcache coherent. UI defaults via onchange: enabling session timeout seeds 1440 min (1 day) + MFA required; enabling inactivity timeout seeds 15 min + MFA off.

On a CheckIdentityException, _handle_error redirects HTTP requests to /auth-timeout/check-identity (server-rendered page) while JSONRPC errors surface as the screen-lock dialog. The /auth-timeout/session/check-identity jsonrpc route calls ir.http._check_identity(credential): with no credential it returns the user's available _get_auth_methods (webauthn/totp/totp_mail/password); with a credential it runs user._check_credentials, and when the breached timeout demanded MFA and more than one method exists it records the first factor in session 'identity-check-1fa' and asks for a second. On success it pops 'identity-check-next' and stamps 'identity-check-last', clearing the deadline. auth_totp.device._get_trusted_device_age is also capped to the shortest MFA session timeout so a 'remembered' device can't outlive the policy.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (CheckIdentity OWL dialog + error handler, static)
behavioral_notes.observation: Client footprint is a small OWL surface, not a Python concern: components CheckIdentityDialog and CheckIdentityForm, a 'check_identity' service, a 'checkIdentityErrorHandler' error_handler (catches the CheckIdentityException over rpc and pops the screen-lock dialog instead of erroring), and a public_components registration 'auth_timeout.check_identity_form' for the standalone page. Bundles touched: web.assets_backend (1), web.assets_frontend (2), web.assets_tests (1); 1 JS file + 1 QWeb template (the check_identity page). The web client also reads 'lock_timeout_inactivity' injected into session_info/get_frontend_session_info to drive the inactivity countdown locally.

it_architecture.application: auth_timeout (session inactivity / max-age timeout: lazily re-confirms identity or logs out idle or long-lived web sessions, with optional MFA step-up, layered on the web request dispatch)
software_services: /auth-timeout/check-identity (HTTP: server-rendered re-auth page reached on CheckIdentityException redirect)
/auth-timeout/session/check-identity (JSONRPC: receive the screen-lock auth form, run _check_identity)
/web/webclient/load_menus (re-routed check_identity=False so the bare fetch is exempt from the gate)
data_objects: (none - models=0; behaviour lives in ir.http / ir.websocket / res.groups / res.users extensions and HTTP session keys)
logical_data_erm: res.groups -1::N(implied)-> res.users (timeout policy resolved from implied-group membership)
res.users -reads-> res.groups._get_lock_timeouts (shortest per-type timeout, MFA vs non-MFA)
HTTP session keys: create_time / identity-check-next / identity-check-last / identity-check-1fa (transient state, no DB table)
information_flows: depends: auth_totp + auth_totp_mail + auth_passkey (re-auth offers totp/totp_mail/webauthn/password factors) + bus (websocket presence carries inactivity)
stamp: web client presence -> ir.websocket._update_mail_presence -> ir.http._set_session_inactivity -> session['identity-check-next'] (saved to session_store)
arm-on-close: ir.websocket._on_websocket_closed(force=True) -> identity-check-next set immediately (last tab closed / connection lost)
gate: every auth='user' request -> ir.http._authenticate -> _must_check_identity -> compare now vs create_time (age) & identity-check-next (idle)
logout: lock_timeout breached -> SessionExpiredException -> client redirect to /web/login (full re-login)
lock: lock_timeout_inactivity breached -> CheckIdentityException -> _handle_error -> /auth-timeout/check-identity (page) or screen-lock dialog (rpc)
re-auth: /auth-timeout/session/check-identity -> _check_identity -> _check_credentials (+optional MFA step-up via identity-check-1fa) -> pop identity-check-next, set identity-check-last
config: res.groups timeout fields -> _get_lock_timeouts (ormcache, cleared on create/write/unlink) -> res.users -> session_info/get_frontend_session_info (lock_timeout_inactivity to JS countdown)
frontend_components: CheckIdentityDialog (OWL screen-lock dialog shown on CheckIdentityException over rpc)
CheckIdentityForm (OWL re-auth form, also registered as public_components auth_timeout.check_identity_form)

capabilities: Session Inactivity Timeout (auto screen-lock after idle period)
Maximum Session Age / Forced Re-login (regardless of activity)
Lazy Identity Re-confirmation on Request Dispatch
Step-up Multi-Factor Re-authentication (optional MFA on timeout)
Group-scoped Timeout Policy Configuration (per access group, shortest-wins)
Trusted-Device Age Capping to Session Policy
value_streams: Idle-to-Locked: presence reports inactivity -> identity-check-next armed -> next request raises CheckIdentityException -> screen-lock dialog -> re-auth -> session resumed
Aged-to-Relogin: session passes lock_timeout from create_time -> next request raises SessionExpiredException -> redirect to /web/login -> full re-login
Policy-to-Enforcement: admin sets group lock_timeout(_inactivity) -> _get_lock_timeouts cache rebuilt -> every member's sessions gated
information_concepts: HTTP session deadline keys (create_time, identity-check-next, identity-check-last, identity-check-1fa)
resolved per-user timeouts ((seconds, requires_mfa) tuples from _get_lock_timeouts)
policies: Timeout policy is attached to res.groups, not per-user; the SHORTEST timeout across all implied groups wins (stricter group dominates)
Two independent thresholds: hard max session age (lock_timeout vs create_time) and idle period (lock_timeout_inactivity vs identity-check-next)
Each timeout can independently require MFA (lock_timeout_mfa / lock_timeout_inactivity_mfa); UI defaults: 1 day + MFA for session, 15 min no-MFA for inactivity
Enforcement is lazy/at-dispatch (next request after the deadline), not a background expiry job
Routes may opt out of the identity check via routing check_identity=False (e.g. the re-auth routes themselves and /web/webclient/load_menus)
Trusted-device (auth_totp.device) lifetime is capped to the shortest MFA session timeout so 'remember me' cannot outlive policy
stakeholders: End user / employee (sees the screen-lock dialog and re-authenticates after idling)
Security administrator (sets per-group session and inactivity timeouts + MFA requirements)
Compliance / IT governance owner (relies on auto-lock to meet unattended-session controls)
Module developer (consumes _must_check_identity / check_identity=False routing flag and the auth-method extension points)
metrics: count of groups with lock_timeout / lock_timeout_inactivity configured (policy coverage)
frequency of CheckIdentityException / SessionExpiredException (re-auth and forced-logout rate)
shortest effective timeout per user (strictness of applied policy)

classification.rationale: auth_timeout is IT security infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'). It owns NO business object of its own (models=0: every piece of behaviour is an extension of ir.http, ir.websocket, res.groups and res.users plus transient HTTP-session keys), so it cannot be chain/shop/network. Its sole purpose is session-lifecycle hardening: lazily re-confirming identity or logging out idle / long-lived web sessions that EVERY other module sits behind. It creates no document chain, holds no customer/order/product/ledger data, and produces no primary-activity output. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' is the precise fit - specifically the 'Develop and manage IT security, privacy and data protection' / identity & access management capability, here the concrete runtime build/run of an access control (inactivity + max-age timeout, MFA step-up, group-scoped policy) wired into the request dispatcher. 11.0 'Manage Enterprise Risk, Compliance, Remediation and Resiliency' was considered because auto-lock supports unattended-session compliance mandates, but rejected: 11.0 is the governance layer (risk registers, control frameworks, audits, policy management) whereas auth_timeout is the technical implementation IT operates and delivers. No row exists in apqc_odoo_map.tsv for auth_timeout (that map enumerates primary chain/shop activities only); aligned instead with the auth_totp sibling record, which is likewise 8.0/support.

standard_capabilities: Inactivity timeout (auto screen-lock) after a configurable idle period, enforced at the next request
Maximum session age forcing full re-login independent of activity
Optional MFA step-up on either timeout (reuse of auth_totp / auth_totp_mail / auth_passkey factors)
Group-scoped timeout policy with shortest-applicable-timeout resolution across implied groups
Presence-driven inactivity tracking over the bus websocket, with immediate arming on tab/connection close
Screen-lock OWL dialog for rpc requests + server-rendered re-auth page for plain HTTP requests
Trusted-device age automatically capped to the session MFA timeout
typical_fits: Locking unattended back-office sessions after N minutes idle to meet security/compliance controls
Forcing a daily full re-login on sensitive groups (default 1-day session timeout + MFA)
Requiring a second factor when an admin group session times out, without re-typing the password elsewhere
Applying stricter timeouts to admin/finance groups while leaving ordinary users looser (shortest-wins)
common_gaps: Configuration is per access group only - no per-user or single global system-parameter timeout out of the box
Enforcement is lazy (on next request) - a truly idle tab is only locked when it next talks to the server
Inactivity detection depends on the bus websocket presence channel; environments that block websockets weaken idle tracking
No built-in audit log / report of lock & forced-logout events (only the exceptions in the request log)
No UI to configure timeouts per individual user; relies on group membership modelling
